overview: AWS infrastructure is organised into Regions, each made of isolated Availability Zones built from data centers, plus edge locations close to users. Choosing a Region and spreading across AZs underpins every availability, latency and compliance question.

coreConcepts.definition: A geographic area containing a cluster of data centers, named like us-east-1 or eu-west-3.
One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity inside a Region.
A site close to end users that delivers content with lower latency.
A service not tied to one Region, such as IAM, Route 53, CloudFront and WAF.
A service whose resources live in one Region, such as EC2, Elastic Beanstalk, Lambda and Rekognition.

mustRemember: A Region usually has 3 AZs: minimum 3, maximum 6.
AZ names add a letter to the Region name, e.g. ap-southeast-2a.
AZs are isolated from each other but linked with high-bandwidth, ultra-low-latency networking.
Data never leaves a Region without your explicit permission.
Not every service or feature is available in every Region.
Pricing varies from Region to Region.
AWS has 400+ Points of Presence in 90+ cities across 40+ countries.

keyComparisons.difference: A Region is a geographic area; an AZ is an isolated set of data centers inside it.
AZs run your workloads; edge locations cache and deliver content near users.
Global services such as IAM span all Regions; EC2 resources exist in one Region.

commonMisunderstandings: An Availability Zone is not a Region; each Region contains multiple AZs.
An AZ is not always a single building; it is one or more data centers.
Launching in any Region does not guarantee every service is available there.
mentalModels: Region = city, AZ = separate neighbourhoods with their own power, edge location = local delivery point.
Spreading across AZs protects against a single-site disaster inside one Region.
edgeCases: A Region has at least 3 AZs, so multi-AZ designs are always possible within one Region.

whenToUse.situation: Data must stay in a specific country by law
whenToUse.use: A Region in that jurisdiction (compliance first)

whenToUse.situation: Users are concentrated in one geography
whenToUse.use: The Region closest to them for lower latency
Check it is available in the target Region

examTraps.trap: An Availability Zone contains multiple Regions
IAM users must be created per Region
Pick the cheapest Region even if data residency rules apply
